lectures.title: Software Version Control with DNF Modules for Ensuring Stability (Part 2)

cues.en: We have now already seen quite a bit about modules, but there are quite a few more commands that I
would like to introduce you to.
We could, for example, also install a module directly and here we can say DNF module install and then
the name of the module.
Or we can also specify the name, the stream and with a slash, also the profile that we would like
to install.
Or we could even just do DNF install and then use the add here to indicate that we want to refer to
a module.
I would like to emphasize here the profile.
It's all part of the same stream.
So we are subscribed to the stream, but by installing a specific profile there, we then install all
the packages associated to that profile.
So we get a nice preset of installed packages on our system through this profile feature.
What's up with that profile?
So let's have a look at this sudo DNF module list.
Let's list our modules and here we can see in the third column that we can that we have multiple profiles
available.
We just installed the common profile here.
But let's say, for example, we want to install the development profile here.
It's not like the way it works is that we subscribe to a module with a module name and a stream, and
the profile defines which packages should be installed by default.
So we just installed the common profile of Node, and those are just the common tools, but we could
also install the development profile here.
So I could say sudo DNF module install and we want to install the NodeJS module at version 18.
And then the development profile.
By the way, this one here, we could also leave out.
Then it would just take the first one here.
That one would work as well, but this would be the most specific way to install that module.
And now when I scroll up here, you can see that because we selected a different profile, we are installing
a different package here.
That's all part of that module that we enabled.
But it's a different package here and this makes sure that all the development tools are being installed
as well.
And we can see here it's a little bit more that we now need to download and install.
It's actually not that much, but this would be then the development profile of that module.
So I will now just confirm this one.
And as we can see here, a few seconds later, it has installed successfully so we can see how we can
directly install a module.
We have seen here that we can just install a specific profile.
And this profile, if we, for example, installed this development profile here for NodeJS, it came
with a certain set of software that was then installed or also this common profile also came with a
certain set of software that was then installed.
So this one here was the module name and the stream that we subscribed to.
And this one here we are then pretty much like starting package sets.
We can see a little bit like that that had been installed when we installed a specific profile here.
If we want to uninstall a specific profile, we can do this with DNF module remove.
This will not remove the module, it will just remove the profile and we can specify the name of the
module.
Or we can also specify the name of the profile with a slash here.
Or we could also say colon and then the stream number to be even more expressive here.
And we can also add the minus minus all flag, and this will then uninstall all software that was provided
by this module.
We should have a look at that as an example.
So here you have seen I've installed this development profile and I can just say sudo DNF module, remove
NodeJS, then I specify the version and then I say development and this will not remove the NodeJS module.
It will just uninstall this profile.
So if I now hit enter, we can see all of this software had been installed when I installed the development
profile and all of those dependencies and all of that will now be removed.
But I'm still subscribed if we see it here.
I'm still subscribed here to the NodeJS 18 stream.
We can see it here that this stream is still enabled.
So the stream is still on our system.
So this remove command wasn't uninstalling the module itself.
It was just uninstalling this profile that we had installed.
And by uninstalling that profile, all of those other tools that have been installed through that profile
will be removed.
We can also say sudo DNF module remove minus, minus all NodeJS.
And what this one will do is that it will check all the software that is provided by that module and
it will try to remove all of that.
And if we see it here, this would then, for example, mean that we would uninstall NodeJS, NodeJS
docs and all of those software would then be removed.
If we were to execute this one, I will now decline that one because I still want NodeJS to be installed
for now.
We can also disable a module.
This will mean that the software will remain installed, but the module streams will become unavailable,
so we will no longer subscribe to updates there.
And we could do that with DNF module disable for a specific name.
We can have a look at that one.
I just go here sudo DNF module, disable nodejs and then we can see here.
This module will now be disabled.
I confirm this sudo DNF module list and we can see here that this module is now disabled, so we are
no longer subscribing to any updates there.
But if I now say node dash dash version, we can see I've still version 18 installed here on my system.
How can we reset a module?
Well, this will reset the stream and the profile to the default and but we need to be aware that this
doesn't uninstall the software, it just changes the configuration here in a sense that this module
will neither be activated nor or it will neither be enabled nor disabled.
It will be completely removed, that module here from our system.
But it doesn't affect the software.
So we can say sudo DNF module reset for a specific module and this will then reset that module for us.
Here.
In my case, it's a little bit more complicated.
When we see the DNF module list, we can see here that we got those NodeJS module and we can see that

So I could now just try to remove this one.

In that version here we can just remove this profile here, um, by with the DNF module, remove command.

So here in this case, this remove will not remove this nodejs and all I could do would be sudo DNF

This will then at least reset my module configuration.
It will still not downgrade my node.
So if I would see here sudo DNF module list, we can see now that this NodeJS module is neither enabled
nor disabled nor anything here.
This is now just back to the previous state.
But we still got the problem because NodeJS had been installed before.
I enabled that module.
If I would now execute Node ID, we would see that it's here still in version 18.
By the way.
The reason why it's not deleting that is that it's marked and on the system how a software has been
installed and it's not marked as a dependency or anything like this.
So it can't just uninstall it and it also can't just downgrade it so it just stays installed.
So we now need to manually take care of that.
But the easiest way would be sudo DNF module, remove dash, dash, all NodeJS and that would then uninstall
everything here.
We now got the little bit of the problem that this one no longer works if that module is no longer active.
So in our case it's actually that we need to install that module first, install the module NodeJS.
Now it's installed.
Now I can remove all the software that comes from that module stream.
Remove dash.
Dash.
All.
I now uninstall everything that's in that module stream.
I confirm this with a Y and now I could say sudo DNF module reset nodejs and now this module will be

Now Node has been uninstalled and now I can say sudo DNF install NodeJS.
So it's a little bit tricky here what we needed to do, but now we are finally back at version 16.
So what we needed to do here is we needed to enable that module again that we have access to the module
stream.
Then we had to manually remove everything that was associated to that module and then we could finally
reset that module and the software had been uninstalled and then we could install the software again.
But then with the previous version from our repository.
So disabling and uninstalling a module can be a little bit tricky, especially if the software had been
installed before the module was enabled and before we installed the profile there.
But we can see it's still working and it's still possible to do this.
So this is how modules work and how you can utilize them to install and request specific versions of
